name: Globe and Mail cryptic crossword No 3,372

entries.clue: Horrible, liquid food almost finished by a few (8)

indicatorNotes.almost: almost the whole word: the last letter is dropped
indicatorNotes.finished by: the second piece comes at the end

blocks.note: GRUEL, a thin liquid food, minus its last letter
some = a few

annotation.surface: A diner recoils from a bowl of watery slop, finished off by only a few brave souls.
annotation.walkthrough: The comma after 'Horrible' makes it look like a comment on the food; it is the definition standing alone.
annotation.definitionFit: Something gruesome is horrible, causing revulsion.

entries.clue: New indoor carpet is included (12)

indicatorNotes.New: a new version of the letters: they are rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 12 letters

annotation.surface: A home-improvement listing boasting that new indoor carpeting comes with the house.
annotation.walkthrough: 'New' reads as an adjective describing the carpet, but it tells you to rearrange the two words after it.
annotation.definitionFit: Something incorporated has been included as part of a whole.

entries.clue: Calm sales agent boasted from time to time (6)

indicatorNotes.from time to time: only now and then: every other letter is taken

blocks.note: a rep is a sales representative
the 2nd, 4th and 6th letters of bOaStEd

annotation.surface: A cool, composed salesman who only occasionally brags about his figures.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Calm' looks like an adjective for the sales agent; here it is a noun, the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the noun calm, meaning stillness or tranquillity, is exactly what repose means.

entries.clue: Stick publicity material in this place (6)

blocks.note: an ad is an advertisement
here = in this place

annotation.surface: An instruction to put up a poster on this particular spot.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stick' reads as the imperative 'put up'; it is the verb meaning to cling fast.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the verb stick, as glue sticks to paper, matches the answer.

entries.clue: Result of food fight in military dining hall? (4)

blocks.note: thrown food leaves chaos and dirt behind
the armed forces' word for their communal canteen

annotation.surface: Soldiers hurl their dinners across the canteen, leaving it a wreck.
annotation.walkthrough: MESS is both the chaos and the canteen, so the two meanings sit together as one scene.
annotation.definitionFit: Double definition: the chaos left behind by thrown food, and the name the armed forces give their canteen.

entries.clue: Colour of old stove (6)

blocks.note: O is a standard abbreviation for old
a range is a large cooking stove

annotation.surface: Someone asks what shade an antique cooker was painted.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Colour of old stove' sounds like a paint description; 'of' only links the definition to the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the answer is one particular colour, the shade of the fruit.

entries.clue: Rubbish tee shot heading for lake (6)

indicatorNotes.heading for: the head, or first letter, of the next word

blocks.note: in golf, the long shot off the tee is a drive
first letter of lake

annotation.surface: A golfer's awful opening shot sails straight toward the water hazard.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rubbish' looks like a verdict on the shot; it is the definition, a noun meaning nonsense.
annotation.definitionFit: Drivel is rubbish, silly talk or nonsense.

entries.clue: Non-scientist weirdly playing fast and loose (12)

annotation.definitionNote: The definition is a verb phrase describing behaviour; INCONSISTENT is the adjective for it.

indicatorNotes.weirdly: in a weird arrangement: the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 12 letters

annotation.surface: A layperson behaving oddly, bending the rules of evidence.
annotation.walkthrough: The hyphen is ignored; all twelve letters of 'Non-scientist' are rearranged.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone playing fast and loose is unreliable and inconsistent in their conduct.

entries.clue: Single river heading west in US city (4)

indicatorNotes.heading west: in an across answer, west is right to left: the letters run backwards

blocks.note: one = single
R is a standard abbreviation for river

annotation.surface: A lone river flows westward toward an American town.
annotation.walkthrough: Reno is a city in Nevada.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the answer is one particular city, in Nevada, known for casinos and quick divorces.

entries.clue: Dreary, accomplished performers (8)

blocks.note: over = done, accomplished
the cast is the set of performers in a show

annotation.surface: A dull review of a skilled but lifeless troupe of actors.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Accomplished' suggests skilful; the sense needed is finished, as in 'the game is over'.
annotation.definitionFit: Dreary here describes weather: a sky fully covered by grey cloud is gloomy and dull.

entries.clue: Total struggle to cross line (8)

indicatorNotes.to cross: the word goes across the other, straddling it on both sides

blocks.note: compete = struggle, contend
L is a standard abbreviation for line

annotation.surface: A hard fight to get over the finishing line.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cross' suggests getting over a line; here the struggle straddles the line, holding it inside.
annotation.definitionFit: Complete and total both mean entire, absolute.

entries.clue: Characters winding up arrogant people on X (3)

indicatorNotes.Characters winding up: the letters that wind up, or end, each word

blocks.note: last letters of arrogaNT peoplE oN

annotation.surface: Online trolls baiting self-important users on the social network X.
annotation.walkthrough: X is the Roman numeral for ten; the surface wants it to be the social media platform.
annotation.definitionFit: A crossword staple: the Roman numeral X stands for the number.

entries.clue: Shelter made of some fine sticks? (4)

indicatorNotes.some: only some of the letters of the next words are used

blocks.note: hidden in fiNE STicks

annotation.surface: A bird's home woven from delicate twigs.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface doubles as a description of the answer, since a nest really is built from fine sticks.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in a narrow sense: the shelter a bird builds for its eggs.

entries.clue: Hurry and deal with creepy-crawly? (4,2,2)

blocks.note: an informal order to go faster, from pressing the accelerator pedal
one way to deal with a bug: tread on the thing

annotation.surface: Someone urged to be quick and squash an insect.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second, literal reading of a common idiom.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom meaning hurry up, which read literally is also how you squash a bug.

entries.clue: Beloved person each doctor nurses (4)

indicatorNotes.nurses: to nurse is to hold close: one piece holds the other

blocks.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor
ea is the abbreviation for each

annotation.surface: A cherished figure is a doctor who tends to every patient.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nurses' sits naturally beside 'doctor' in a medical scene, but it means holds, as you nurse a drink.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a darling or loved one, the noun sense of the word, not the adjective.

entries.clue: Impressive and popular, as many churches are (8)

blocks.note: in = fashionable, popular
many churches have spires

annotation.surface: Praise for church architecture that is both grand and well-loved.
annotation.walkthrough: 'As many churches are' is a cryptic pointer to the adjective SPIRED.
annotation.definitionFit: An inspired performance or idea is impressive, brilliantly good.

entries.clue: Bestow one politician with sculpture, perhaps (6)

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
MP = Member of Parliament
sculpture is one kind of art; 'perhaps' marks an example

annotation.surface: An award ceremony presenting a statue to a member of parliament.
annotation.walkthrough: 'With' only joins the definition to the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean to give or grant, often knowledge or a quality.

entries.clue: Make your home somewhere in the Yorkshire Dales (6)

blocks.note: to take up residence somewhere
a small market town in the Dales, a national park in northern England

annotation.surface: Advice to move to a spot in the English countryside.
annotation.walkthrough: The Yorkshire Dales are an upland national park in northern England; SETTLE is one of its towns.
annotation.definitionFit: Double definition: the verb for taking up residence, and a small market town in North Yorkshire.

entries.clue: Weakness not hard to detect (4,4)

blocks.note: soft = not hard
to spot is to detect

annotation.surface: A flaw that is easy to find.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Not hard to detect' reads as one phrase meaning easy to notice, but it splits into two separate pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: A soft spot is a weakness, either a vulnerable point or a fondness.

entries.clue: Leaders of one band offended every music producer (4)

indicatorNotes.Leaders of: the letters that lead each word

blocks.note: first letters of One Band Offended Every

annotation.surface: A band's frontmen annoy every record producer they work with.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Music producer' suggests a studio professional; here it is an instrument, which produces music.
annotation.definitionFit: An oboe is a woodwind instrument, something that produces music.

entries.clue: Excessively large plane, for example (4)

blocks.note: too = excessively
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

annotation.surface: A remark about an oversized aircraft.
annotation.walkthrough: The plane is the carpenter's tool for smoothing wood, not an aircraft.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the carpenter's plane, for smoothing wood, is one kind of hand implement.

entries.clue: Lodger deprived of a bed (6)

indicatorNotes.deprived of: the next piece is taken away

blocks.note: a boarder pays for room and meals
the letter A is removed

annotation.surface: A tenant left without anywhere to sleep.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bed' suggests sleeping, but it is a garden bed; a border is a flower bed along the edge of a lawn.
annotation.definitionFit: A border is a strip of garden bed planted with flowers.

entries.clue: Leguminous plant close to coastal inlet flourished (6)

indicatorNotes.close to: the close, or end, of the next word
indicatorNotes.flourished: waved about with a flourish: the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: last letter of coastal
INLET rearranged

annotation.surface: A bean plant growing well beside a seaside creek.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Close to' reads as 'near'; here it means the close, or last letter, of 'coastal'.
annotation.definitionFit: The lentil is a legume grown for its edible seeds.
